title: Witsoc-2 domain pack manifest
description: The five-item contract a domain pack must satisfy to plug into the Witsoc-2 frame. Every field here is frame-owned; the values are domain-owned. See references/domain_pack_contract.md.

contract_version.description: Which version of the five-item contract this pack implements. Governance rule 6: packs declare it, the frame never infers it.

domain.description: Pack identifier. Must match its directory name under domains/. A leading underscore marks a frame fixture rather than a real field; check_frame_purity.py uses the same convention to decide what a frame file may reference.

roles.description: Optional domain-specific names for the three protected roles. The mapping must stay one-to-one; a pack may rename a role but may not add or drop one. Omit to use the frame names.

verification_adapter.description: CONTRACT ITEM 1. A function (candidate artifact) -> (pass/fail, receipt). May dispatch over several backends internally; the frame only sees the signature.

entry_point.description: Command or module path the frame invokes. Receives an artifact reference, returns a frame-receipt-v1.

tiers.description: One entry per verification backend, cheapest first. A single-backend domain declares one tier. A domain spanning symbolic/simulated/physical checking declares several; Explorer freezes which tier a claim requires before Generator starts.

adversarial.description: True only if this backend cannot be talked into a false pass, in which case a single run of it satisfies the refute-attempt gate. Graded or sampling-based backends are false, and must earn a receipt through a separate refute-attempt (see gates.refute_attempt).

cost_hint.description: Relative expense, used by Explorer for tier selection only. Never affects acceptance.

max_status.description: The strongest status a pass on this tier can EVER support. Separate from `adversarial`, which the frame previously conflated with it: an exhaustive search over a stated finite domain is genuinely adversarial — it cannot be argued into a false pass — and still establishes nothing outside its bounds. Discharging the refute-attempt gate does not lift this ceiling.

two_sided_evidence.description: Evidence that this tier returns fail on inputs that should fail. A backend nothing has ever failed is unaudited, not trustworthy. Required in spirit for any tier claiming adversarial:true.

authorship.description: Who wrote this backend relative to whoever produces candidates for it. 'independent' is the only value that supports adversarial:true.

contamination_controls.description: How material this tier evaluates against is kept from being visible to, or fitted by, the producer.

availability_check.description: Cheap command or probe reporting whether this tier can run at all right now. Lets a run state an honest ceiling up front instead of discovering unavailability after the budget is gone.

negative_control.description: Path to a known-BAD artifact this tier must reject. Re-run at registration, it converts adversarial:true from a self-report by the party being checked into a test.

prefix_reuse.description: Whether this backend can load expensive shared setup once and fork each branch from that snapshot. Where available this is the largest single speedup in a verification pipeline — an order of magnitude, not a percentage.

concurrency_limit.description: Maximum concurrent invocations of this tier. Memory- or licence-bound backends saturate; the frame queues rather than stacking past this.

corpus.description: CONTRACT ITEM 1b. The domain's knowledge/retrieval substrate. Explorer is required to 'retrieve against the domain corpus', so a pack needs somewhere to declare one — without this slot the frame mandates an operation whose substrate it gives no way to supply.

version.description: Pinned corpus version. A retrieval result is only reproducible against a stated version.

claim_schema.description: CONTRACT ITEM 2. The structured, frozen representation of what is being claimed. Extends the frame's generic claim with domain-specific fields.

path.description: Path to the domain's claim schema, relative to the pack directory.

additional_required_fields.description: Domain-specific fields this pack adds on top of the frame claim.

receipt_format.description: CONTRACT ITEM 3. What counts as a receipt in this field, and when one goes stale.

required_fields.description: Fields that must be present for a receipt to be admissible.

freshness_rule.description: Required, and required to be non-trivial. A receipt produced before the artifact's last edit is not evidence about the artifact that exists now. State how staleness is detected in this domain.

doctrine.description: CONTRACT ITEM 4. Field-specific rules layered on the frame's generic doctrine.

escalation.description: The domain's parameters for the frame-owned escalation ladder. The counter and ladder live in the frame; only these values are domain-owned. See references/failure_recovery.md.

max_consecutive_failures.description: N. After N consecutive Generator failures on the same frozen claim, the frame escalates to Researcher. Not a suggestion and not a judgment call.

failure_signature.description: How this domain decides two failures are 'the same failure'. A repeat of an identical signature triggers escalation even before N is reached.

rules.description: Paths to this pack's doctrine documents, relative to the pack directory.

roles.description: Per-role doctrine. When a claim in this field is routed, each general role loads its entry here and operates under it — that is the whole mechanism by which a field's instructions reach the roles. Required, because a pack whose roles have no instructions cannot actually be worked.

explorer.description: How Explorer freezes, falsifies, retrieves, and picks a tier in this field.

generator.description: How Generator produces, submits, and repairs in this field.

researcher.description: How Researcher attacks an obstruction in this field.

gates.description: CONTRACT ITEM 5. The checks a candidate artifact must pass before its status may move off CONJECTURE.

refute_attempt.description: Required, so no pack can skip it by omission. The named gate whose only job is to try to break a passing result. Where a tier is already adversarial this names that tier; otherwise it names a perturbed re-run or a dedicated skeptic pass. A result surviving only one favorable run does not earn a receipt.

satisfied_by_tier.description: Name of an adversarial tier that discharges this gate on its own. Omit when the gate is a separate step.

additional.description: Other domain gates: placeholder scans, tampering diffs, threshold checks, correction procedures.

blocking.description: Whether failing this gate blocks admission outright. Defaults to true.

status_refinements.description: Substrate-specific refinements of the frame statuses this pack registers, e.g. VERIFIED_<substrate>. status_vocabulary.md says a pack may register these; this is the slot it registers them in.
